html:
The Karangura are an Aboriginal people recorded in the far north of South Australia, in the channel country of the lower Diamantina River north of Lake Eyre.

Their neighbours on the map include the Wangkangurru of the Simpson Desert, the Ngamini and the Yarluyandi. Peoples of this region were linked by trade routes that carried pituri, a native tobacco, and red ochre over long distances. Little is recorded about the Karangura as a separate group. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Karangura are an Aboriginal people recorded in the far north of South Australia, in the channel country of the lower Diamantina River north of Lake Eyre.
